```{r aggregated psi medians}
# 1. Install and load necessary packages
# The 'parallel' package is usually pre-installed with R
library(data.table)
library(parallel) 
library(tidyverse)# For parallel processing

# --- Define the function to process a single file (no change needed here) ---
process_psi_file <- function(file_path) {
    # 1. Extract the gene name from the directory path
    # Assuming the structure is: /path/to/gene_name/psi_table.tsv
    gene_name <- basename(dirname(file_path))

    # 2. Read the file efficiently (fread is very fast)
    # The first column is sample_id, which we don't need for the calculation
    # We specify sep="\t" and skip empty files check
    psi_dt <- tryCatch(
        fread(file_path, data.table = T) %>%
          column_to_rownames('V1'),
        error = function(e) {
            # Return NULL if there's an error (e.g., file exists but is corrupted or truly empty)
            return(NULL)
        }
    )

    # 3. Check if the file was read successfully and is not effectively empty
    if (is.null(psi_dt) || ncol(psi_dt) <= 1 || nrow(psi_dt) == 0) {
        message(paste("Skipping empty or malformed file:", file_path))
        return(NULL)
    }


    # 5. Calculate the median PSI for each column (junction)
    # The 'apply' function is efficient for column-wise operations on data.tables/matrices.
    # We ignore NAs automatically using na.rm = TRUE.
    median_psis <- apply(psi_dt, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)

    # 6. Extract the junction details from the column names
    # Column names are in the format: clu_id:start-end
    junction_names <- names(psi_dt)
    
    # Split the names to get start and end
    # Example: "CLU0001:100-200" -> split on ":" -> second part "100-200"
    start_end_parts <- sub(".*:", "", junction_names)
    
    # Split the start-end part on "-"
    split_coords <- tstrsplit(start_end_parts, split = "-", fixed = TRUE)
    start_coords <- as.integer(split_coords[[1]])
    end_coords <- as.integer(split_coords[[2]])

    # 7. Create the final output data.table for this gene
    result_dt <- data.table(
        gene_name = gene_name,
        start = start_coords,
        end = end_coords,
        median_psi = median_psis
    )

    return(result_dt)
}

# --- Main execution block (PARALLELIZED) ---

# 1. Find all 'psi_table.tsv' files
all_files <- list.files(
    path = "../leafcutter_analyses/psi_files/tcga",
    pattern = "psi_table.tsv",
    recursive = TRUE,
    full.names = TRUE
)

message(paste("Found", length(all_files), "files to process."))

# 2. Setup the parallel environment
# Detect the number of available CPU cores
num_cores <- detectCores()
# Use one less core than detected to leave one core free for system tasks
use_cores <- max(1, num_cores - 1) 
message(paste("Starting cluster with", use_cores, "cores."))

# Create a cluster (a set of R processes)
cl <- makeCluster(use_cores)

# Load the 'data.table' package on each worker node
clusterEvalQ(cl, {
    library(data.table)
    library(tidyverse)
})

# Export the processing function to each worker node
clusterExport(cl, "process_psi_file")

# 3. Process all files using parLapply (parallel version of lapply)
# This is where the file reading and processing happens in parallel
final_output_list <- parLapply(cl, all_files, process_psi_file)

# Stop the cluster when done
stopCluster(cl)
message("Cluster stopped.")

# 4. Combine the results efficiently
final_output_dt <- rbindlist(final_output_list, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)

# 5. Write the final data.table to a file
output_file_name <- "aggregated_psi_medians.tsv"

if (nrow(final_output_dt) > 0) {
    fwrite(
        final_output_dt,
        file = output_file_name,
        sep = "\t",
        quote = FALSE,
        row.names = FALSE
    )
    message(paste("✅ Successfully created the output file:", output_file_name))
} else {
    message("❌ No valid data was processed. Output file was not created.")
}
```


```{r junction rpm medians}
gene_table <- fread('../inputs/snaptron/tcga/chr1/snaptron_output/ABCA4_snaptron.tsv')
tcga_metadata <- fread('../inputs/tcga_v2_samples.tsv', data.table = F)

junction_coverage <- select(tcga_metadata, c(rail_id, junction_coverage))
junction_coverage$rail_id <- as.character(junction_coverage$rail_id)


# --- IMPORTANT: Placeholder for your existing junction_coverage data ---
# This script ASSUMES a global data.table named 'junction_coverage' exists
# with columns 'rail_id' (character) and 'junction_coverage' (numeric).
# Example structure (replace this with your actual data):
# set.seed(42)
# junction_coverage <- data.table(
#     rail_id = paste0("rail_", 1001:1005),
#     junction_coverage = runif(5, 500000, 1000000)
# )
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Define the function to process a single gene directory ---
process_gene_data <- function(dat_file_path, junction_coverage) {
    # 1. Extract the gene name from the directory path
    gene_dir <- dirname(dat_file_path)
    gene_name <- basename(gene_dir)
    
    message(paste("Processing gene:", gene_name))


    # 3. Read sample IDs (rail_ids) from res.RDS
    rail_ids <- tryCatch({
        as.character(fread(dat_file_path, data.table = F) %>%
            .$V1)
    }, error = function(e) {
        message(paste("Skipping gene:", gene_name, "- Failed to read valid rail_ids from dat.tsv. Error:", e$message))
        return(NULL)
    })
    if (is.null(rail_ids)) return(NULL)

    # 4. Read the junction reads data from dat.tsv
    reads_dt <- tryCatch(
        # Note: dat.tsv has no header for the first column (which is V1 in fread)
        fread(dat_file_path, data.table = TRUE),
        error = function(e) {
            message(paste("Skipping gene:", gene_name, "- Failed to read dat.tsv. Error:", e$message))
            return(NULL)
        }
    )
    
    # 5. Validate the reads data and assign rail_ids
    if (is.null(reads_dt) || ncol(reads_dt) < 1 || nrow(reads_dt) != length(rail_ids)) {
        message(paste("Skipping gene:", gene_name, "- Reads data mismatch (rows:", nrow(reads_dt), ", expected:", length(rail_ids), ")."))
        return(NULL)
    }

    # Assign rail_ids as the first column (the sample identifier)
    reads_dt <- dplyr::select(reads_dt, -V1)
    reads_dt[, rail_id := rail_ids]
    
    # 6. Merge reads data with global coverage data
    # Ensure correct join key order to keep rail_id as the first column
    setcolorder(reads_dt, c("rail_id", setdiff(names(reads_dt), "rail_id")))

    # Merge reads with coverage data on 'rail_id'
    merged_dt <- merge(reads_dt, junction_coverage, by = "rail_id", all.x = FALSE)

    # Check for successful merge (i.e., we have the necessary coverage column)
    if (!"junction_coverage" %in% names(merged_dt)) {
        message(paste("Skipping gene:", gene_name, "- Failed to find junction_coverage column after merge."))
        return(NULL)
    }
    
    # Identify junction columns (all columns except rail_id and junction_coverage)
    junction_cols <- setdiff(names(merged_dt), c("rail_id", "junction_coverage"))
    if (length(junction_cols) == 0) {
        message(paste("Skipping gene:", gene_name, "- No junction columns found in dat.tsv."))
        return(NULL)
    }

    # 7. Calculate Junction RPM efficiently using data.table (vectorized division)
    # Perform division: Reads / Coverage * 1e6
    for (j in junction_cols) {
        # Using := operator for in-place calculation, avoids copying large data
        merged_dt[, (j) := get(j) / merged_dt[["junction_coverage"]] * 1e6]
    }
    
    # Remove the rail_id and junction_coverage columns to keep only RPM values
    rpm_dt <- merged_dt[, c("rail_id", "junction_coverage") := NULL]

    # 8. Calculate the median RPM for each junction (column)
    # Using 'apply' on the matrix form of the data.table for maximum speed
    median_rpms <- apply(as.matrix(rpm_dt), 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)

    # 9. Extract junction details from column names
    junction_names <- names(rpm_dt)
    
    # Column names are in the format: start-end
    split_coords <- tstrsplit(junction_names, split = "-", fixed = TRUE)
    start_coords <- as.integer(split_coords[[1]])
    end_coords <- as.integer(split_coords[[2]])

    # 10. Create the final output data.table for this gene
    result_dt <- data.table(
        gene_name = gene_name,
        start = start_coords,
        end = end_coords,
        median_rpm = median_rpms
    )

    return(result_dt)
}

# --- Main execution block (PARALLELIZED) ---

# 1. Find all 'dat.tsv' files recursively
# Per-gene junction tables: ../leafcutter_analyses/junction_tables/chr*/<gene>/dat.tsv
base_path <- "../leafcutter_analyses/junction_tables/"
all_dat_files <- list.files(
    path = base_path,
    pattern = "^dat\\.tsv$",
    recursive = TRUE,
    full.names = TRUE
)

message(paste("Found", length(all_dat_files), "files to potentially process."))

# 2. Setup the parallel environment
num_cores <- detectCores()
# Use one less core than detected to leave one core free for system tasks
use_cores <- max(1, num_cores - 1) 
message(paste("Starting cluster with", use_cores, "cores."))

cl <- makeCluster(use_cores)

# 3. Distribute necessary objects and libraries to all worker nodes
clusterEvalQ(cl, {
    library(data.table)
    library(tidyverse)
})
# Export the processing function AND the global 'junction_coverage' data
clusterExport(cl, c("process_gene_data", "junction_coverage"))

# 4. Process all files using parLapply (parallel execution)
# Each core processes a subset of the files simultaneously
final_output_list <- parLapply(cl, all_dat_files, function(file_path) {
    # Call the processing function within the worker context
    process_gene_data(file_path, junction_coverage)
})

# Stop the cluster when done
stopCluster(cl)
message("Cluster stopped.")

# 5. Combine the results efficiently
# Remove NULL entries from the list (files that were skipped)
final_output_list <- final_output_list[!sapply(final_output_list, is.null)]
final_output_dt <- rbindlist(final_output_list, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)

# 6. Write the final data.table to a file
output_file_name <- "aggregated_junction_rpms.tsv"

if (nrow(final_output_dt) > 0) {
    fwrite(
        final_output_dt,
        file = output_file_name,
        sep = "\t",
        quote = FALSE,
        row.names = FALSE
    )
    message(paste("✅ Successfully created the output file:", output_file_name))
} else {
    message("❌ No valid data was processed. Output file was not created.")
}

```
